question.problem: The Philippines is subject to tropical cyclones, with a month-round average frequency of $2.5$ typhoons per month. What is the probability that there will be no more than $2$ typhoons next month? Round your answer to $3$ decimal places. You may assume that typhoons occur independently and at a constant average rate.
question.worked_solution:
A Poisson random variable $X$ with rate $\lambda $ has the following probability mass function:

$$
f(x)=\frac{{\lambda }^{x}{e}^{-\lambda }}{x!}
$$

Let $X$ be the number of typhoons in a month in the Philippines. Since the average rate is $2.5$ typhoons per month, and events occur independently and at a constant average rate, the number of typhoons can be modeled as a Poisson random variable with rate $\lambda =2.5,$ and we can write $X∼\text{Po}(2.5).$ 

So, $X$ has the following probability mass function:

$$
f(x)=\frac{{2.5}^{x}{e}^{-2.5}}{x!}
$$

Therefore, the probability that there will be at most $2$ typhoons next month is

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le 2) & =P(X\in {0,1,2}) \\  & =f(0)+f(1)+f(2) \\  & =\frac{{2.5}^{0}{e}^{-2.5}}{0!}+\frac{{2.5}^{1}{e}^{-2.5}}{1!}+\frac{{2.5}^{2}{e}^{-2.5}}{2!} \\  & ≈0.544\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $3$ decimal places.
